title: UP Cities Get Cleanliness and Lighting Makeover Ahead of Diwali and Chhath
excerpt: CM Yogi Adityanath ordered festival-ready cities — clean roads, working lights, food-safety inspections — as six UP cities join the Centre's Pragati-50 model-cities program.
body:
• Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered a special cleanliness drive across the state's cities ahead of Diwali and Chhath: clean and well-lit roads, prompt waterlogging fixes, uninterrupted power supply, and decorative lighting in urban areas.
  • Six UP cities — Agra, Ayodhya, Lucknow, Mathura-Vrindavan, Prayagraj and Varanasi — were selected under the Centre's Pragati-50 initiative as model cities for cleanliness and modern civic infrastructure; UP has the most cities of any state in the program.
  • The state's food safety department will run expedited inspections against adulteration of milk, sweets and festival food, with traders warned that action against the guilty will be immediate.
  • Diaspora visitors heading to UP for Diwali: Ayodhya's Deepotsav and Varanasi's Dev Deepawali (November 24) are the headline spectacles, and the Pragati-50 cities are the ones getting the heaviest civic attention this season.

The directive from Lucknow

At a high-level review meeting covering Diwali, Chhath and the UPPSC examination, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath instructed municipal bodies and district administrations to deliver festival-ready cities: a special cleanliness drive before the festivals, clean and well-lit roads and lanes, prompt resolution of waterlogging issues, uninterrupted power supply, and installation of decorative spiral lights across urban areas. Coordinated traffic plans are to prevent inconvenience for devotees at major religious sites.

The food-safety arm of the directive is equally pointed. The Food Safety and Drug Administration and district administrations were told to conduct expedited inspections to prevent adulteration of milk, sweets and other festival food items — with the instruction that while traders should not be harassed, action against the guilty must be immediate.

Pragati-50: six UP cities picked

The seasonal cleanup sits inside a larger national push. Six Uttar Pradesh cities — Agra, Ayodhya, Lucknow, Mathura-Vrindavan, Prayagraj and Varanasi — have been selected under the Centre's Pragati-50 initiative, which aims to develop 50 cities across the country as models of cleanliness, modern civic infrastructure and sustainable urban development. Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal Khattar said UP has the highest number of cities among the states selected; the state has also sought the inclusion of Kanpur.

The initiative follows a May PRAGATI review where Prime Minister Narendra Modi directed the urban affairs ministry and states to identify 50 cities and demonstrate comprehensive cleanliness and waste-management outcomes. Under Pragati-50, selected cities get focused attention on 24×7 mechanised cleaning, scientific solid-waste and used-water management, green mobility, solar energy and modern civic amenities.

Kashi's grand stage

The festival capital of the season will be Varanasi. On Dev Deepawali — November 24 this year, the full-moon Kartik Purnima festival — the ghats of Kashi are expected to glow with more than 11 lakh diyas, alongside laser shows and green fireworks. Ahead of the celebration, the ghats along the Ganga are undergoing special cleaning and will be adorned with facade lighting and electric illumination. A four-day Ganga Mahotsav cultural program will run at Rajghat, and a laser show at Chet Singh Ghat will narrate mythological tales of Kashi.

The ground reality check

Announcements are the easy part; last year's Diwali showed the gap. A Times of India reality check in Lucknow found large stretches of the state capital — including parts of Gomtinagar Extension, Rajajipuram, Chowk, Alambagh, and even VIP areas like Hazratganj — still in darkness despite the municipal corporation's claims that all major roads would be illuminated. Residents complained that defunct streetlights made night travel risky, while the civic body said over 5,500 lights had been changed and repairs would be completed in days.

That record is the measure against which this year's orders will be judged. Urban development departments have been asked to run cleanliness campaigns around Dussehra, Diwali and Chhath with daily reporting by sanitation officers, surprise inspections by senior officials, and dustbins in public places — the administrative machinery of a festival the state wants to present as world-class. See The Daily Jagran's meeting report, Webnewswire on Pragati-50, and Curly Tales on Dev Deepawali.

Diaspora angle

For NRIs timing a Diwali trip home, the signal is practical: Ayodhya and Varanasi are getting the heaviest civic investment this season, Dev Deepawali on November 24 extends the festival window beyond Diwali itself, and the food-safety inspections offer some reassurance for the festival sweet-buying. Book accommodation early in Ayodhya and Varanasi — both cities draw lakhs of visitors for the illuminated riverfronts.

What's next

The test is execution over the next two weeks: whether streetlights actually work in Hazratganj this time, whether the cleanliness drives survive beyond the photo opportunities, and whether the Pragati-50 cities start showing the 24×7 mechanised cleaning the program promises. The festival calendar — Diwali, then Chhath, then Dev Deepawali — gives the administration three successive chances to prove it.
